title: Enterprise onboarding triage and eval-gate criteria for model catalog requests
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: We're seeing an increase in enterprise requests to add, pin, and deprecate models in the public catalog. Requests span new open models, customer-provided weights, and version-pinning asks for regulatory reasons. This ticket defines a repeatable triage rubric and concrete eval gates to route requests (self-serve vs. SE-assisted vs. security review) and to prioritize based on enterprise needs (SLAs, data residency, auditability). The goal is a deterministic intake that reduces manual triage time for PM/SE while protecting platform stability and compliance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented intake rubric that can be used by solutions engineers and PMs to classify requests into three buckets: Fast-path (self-serve), SE-assisted onboarding, Enterprise review. 2) A checklist of eval gates with pass/fail thresholds (safety checks, latency overhead, memory footprint, compatibility with private deployments). 3) A prioritization score formula (weighted) that yields a sortable score used in backlog grooming. 4) Playbook links and next-step owners for each bucket. 5) Pilot with 5 recent customer requests to validate routing and timing assumptions.
decisions:
- Use a three-tier routing model: Fast-path, SE-assisted, Enterprise Review.
- Prioritization score will weight: security/compliance (30%), latency/throughput impact (25%), customer revenue/risk (20%), implementation effort (15%), and cross-team dependencies (10%).
- Require security_review for any customer-provided model or requests that demand data residency or on-prem packaging.
- Pin requests: allow short-term pin (<=90 days) via self-serve for hosted catalog if no security flags; long-term pin requires SE-assisted plan and release notes.
- Deprecation: provide 60-day notice for hosted models; enterprise tenants with pinned versions get 180-day support window and migration guidance.
tradeoffs:
- Fast-path increases speed for low-risk models but slightly raises review burden downstream if safety regressions occur.
- Strict eval gates reduce operational risk but increase time-to-onboard and may frustrate smaller teams.
- Weighting prioritizes security/compliance which aligns with enterprise sales but may deprioritize high-growth startup feature requests.
